tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly by the letter: rank 6 > 3 and conditioning ingredients (Cetearyl Alcohol @2, Cetrimonium Chloride @4, Quaternium-18 @5) precede the marker. But the marker is unusually early relative to list length (6 of 34), so the entire marketed payload — Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil @7, five protein species @8/@10/@11/@13/@14, Glycerin @19, Panthenol @20, Sodium PCA @22 — falls in the tail and earns nothing. This is the cohort's most extreme hero-tail structure.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. Every architecture-establishing species outranks the marker - CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, LANOLIN @3, CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 and QUATERNIUM-18 @5 all sit above PARFUM @6 - and the product is a conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1, so the low-water limb does not fire. Earliness alone (rank 6 of 34) is a counter-signal to record, never a disqualification (§3.1.1, 'a merely early marker is still a marker'). The v0.1 reviewer-judgment discomfort about the hero tail is therefore recorded and not acted on. Separately, QUATERNIUM-18 @5 sits at tail_index - 1. RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.3 (E1, 2026-09-14): R3's tail-edge exclusion is WITHDRAWN. A boundary-position species counts normally in every field; what its position costs is confidence, not credit. QUATERNIUM-18 @5 therefore carries S1 in full, conditioning_level returns to `high`, and the value is capped at `moderate` confidence with a `boundary_position_ingredient` hinweise note (see conditioningLevel). Third plausibility limb (E2, §3.1.1) checked and NOT fired: PARFUM @6 is the fragrance compound itself, and its declared allergens BENZYL BENZOATE @31 and LIMONENE @32 sit far BELOW it, which is the ordinally consistent direction.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 dff721bd…), above-tail ranks 1–5; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Re-derived under v0.3 (E1, 2026-09-14). E1 withdraws R3's tail-edge exclusion: a species at tail_index − 1 counts normally and the boundary uncertainty is carried as a confidence cap, not as a value move. QUATERNIUM-18 @5 therefore carries S1 in full alongside CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, S2 is satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, and no material counter-signal fires — so the `high` bar (S1 mandatory plus at least one of S2/S3) is met. Confidence is capped at `moderate` because S1 is load-bearing on a boundary-position species: without QUATERNIUM-18 @5 the value would be `moderate`. This reverses the v0.2 value (`moderate`) and closes AP-01-TAILEDGEDROP in the direction the ruling ledger's 'five evidence-backed highs stand' line implied. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, never measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) — long-chain cationic quat above the tail (tail_index 6, PARFUM): first distinct S1 species

QUATERNIUM-18 (rank 5) — a second, structurally distinct dialkyl cationic quat, declared at tail_index − 1. Under E1 (2026-09-14) it COUNTS in full: relative order above the marker is Art. 19-reliable, only the invisible 1 % line is uncertain, and ~1 % of a co-conditioning quat is a functional dose. It is the species S1 hinges on, and the reason confidence is capped at `moderate`
S1 SATISFIED on those two distinct cationic species; S2 SATISFIED on CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2), a long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three of the full list
LANOLIN (rank 3) — the only non-fatty-alcohol lipid above the tail; ARGANIA SPINOSA KERNEL OIL @7 and ISOPROPYL PALMITATE @21 are in the tail: S3 NOT satisfied (one lipid is not breadth)

PARFUM (rank 6) — tail marker, plausible under §3.1.1 on all three limbs (R2; third limb added E2 — the declared allergens BENZYL BENZOATE @31 and LIMONENE @32 sit below their own PARFUM, which is the consistent ordering)
conditioningLevel.derivation: §9.1 on the above-tail segment (ranks 1–5), under E1's boundary-position rule (no species is removed). S1 = SATISFIED: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 and QUATERNIUM-18 @5, two distinct long-chain cationic species above tail_index 6. S2 = SATISFIED: CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2. S3 = NOT satisfied: LANOLIN @3 is the sole above-tail non-fatty-alcohol lipid. `high` = S1 (mandatory) + at least one of {S2, S3} + no material counter-signal → satisfied via S2. Load-bearing boundary check (E1): removing QUATERNIUM-18 @5 would drop S1 and therefore the value → the species IS load-bearing → confidence capped at `moderate` and `boundary_position_ingredient` emitted.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: §9.1's post-R3 bar is S1 mandatory plus S2 or S3, with no material counter-signal. S1 and S2 both fire and no counter-signal is material. D1's multiple-independent-signals requirement is met by two signals from two different families — cationic breadth (S1) and fatty-alcohol prominence (S2).

`moderate` does not apply, and this is the value that MOVED: it was v0.2's value only because R3's tail-edge exclusion struck QUATERNIUM-18 @5 before the count. E1 withdraws that strike, so the only thing the boundary position now costs is confidence.
`low` does not apply: `low` requires none of S1/S2/S3; two of the three fire.

Material counter-signals (§9.1 closed list) checked and NOT fired: (a) the tail marker is resolved and plausible on all three §3.1.1 limbs; (b) no §2.4.1 tier-2 conflict; (c) no fired signal rests on a lexicon family-10 rheology-only/emulsifier species — both S1 carriers are declared quats and CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 is a fatty alcohol, not a Ceteareth/Glyceryl Stearate blend half.

Confidence is `moderate`, not `high`, under §9.1's E1-amended confidence rule: S1 would not fire without a tail_index − 1 species. Two further independent caps point the same way — the fallback-tier source and the provisional identity conflict — so no single fix would lift it.
counterSignals: The value hinges on one rank: QUATERNIUM-18 @5 against PARFUM @6. Under v0.2's tail-edge exclusion this product read `moderate`; under E1 it reads `high` at capped confidence. Both readings are recorded here so the reviewer can see exactly what the boundary is doing — it is carried as a confidence cap and a `hinweise` note, never as a silent value swing.
The above-tail segment is only five entries; a single transcription slip in a fallback-tier source would change the signal count.

ARGANIA SPINOSA KERNEL OIL @7 and four protein species @8/@10/@11/@13 in the tail are a textbook sub-1 % hero tail — a §9.1 NON-material counter-signal: recorded, never credited, and explicitly not capping.

Lexicon §13's honest caveat applies with full force here: two distinct above-tail cationics is 'near-baseline in this market', so S1's threshold sits low against the German shelf. R3 makes S1 necessary but does not claim it is sufficient — which is why S2 is also required — and whether S1's count should rise to three is §18.1's open calibration question.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support; no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/medium/high thresholds (§9.1 honest limitation).

Rank is used qualitatively only. EU Art. 19 hides the 1 % boundary; no percentage, ratio, dose or deposited amount is inferable. That is precisely the uncertainty E1's confidence cap encodes on this record.
Source is hautschutzengel fallback tier; dm.de is JS-rendered and could not be fetched.

CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — cetearyl-class fatty alcohol within the top three ranks: the dense fatty-alcohol base completer (a)

Completer = (a) dense fatty-alcohol base, satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 within the top three ranks. No material unresolved counter-signal. `moderate` does not apply: `moderate` is everything else once the `high` anchor fails, and the anchor does not fail. Under v0.1 this value hung on a reviewer's R4b reading of lanolin; that hinge is now closed by the lexicon, and AP-01-LANOLIN is closed with it.

`low` does not apply: the leanness test (R4) requires all three of no R4b heavy lipid above the marker, a thin fatty base, and no occlusive silicone stack. Single fallback-tier source; this is what holds confidence at `moderate` rather than `high` now that the lanolin hinge is closed (§4.1: a material input gap).
Lanolin's occlusivity is a well-established formulation property, but the deposited amount from a rinse-out mask is not inferable from an INCI list.
limitations: Weight drives a soft preference with a stated reason, never an exclusion; fine-hair flattening is a fit mismatch, not a hair-type law (§9.2 wording rule).
An ingredient-informed matching prior at E2, never a prediction that the product will visibly flatten hair.

careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test: a qualifying R5 species above the tail is required before either leg (a) or (b) can be considered. There is none, so `protein` is unreachable. §9.3 `balanced` test requires the material R5 route as its first conjunct, so `balanced` is unreachable too. The residual value is `moisture`, which D6 defines as the category's honest default: a coherent conditioning/humectant/emollient architecture without a dominant protein-film route.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture`: the above-tail set is a coherent conditioning/emollient architecture (fatty alcohol + heavy lipid + two cationics) and carries no protein-film route.

`protein` does not apply: it requires a material identifiable R5 route. Zero qualifying R5 species appear above the tail; Silk Amino Acids is additionally excluded as a free amino acid (R5 mask delta).

`balanced` does not apply: D6 reserves it for a substantive mixed protein-plus-moisture architecture and forbids it as a 'neither' bucket. The protein leg is absent, so the reserved value is not available.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R6). `balanced` reading (a) both-substantive is unavailable — no material R5 route above the tail, and no qualifying humectant cluster either (GLYCERIN @19, PANTHENOL @20 and SODIUM PCA @22 are all in the tail). `balanced` reading (b) neither-dominant fails at clause 2: there is no substantive R2 silicone system, no R3 cationic-polymer film and no R6a acid-gloss architecture above the tail — the credited segment is a bare R1 base plus LANOLIN @3. The value is unchanged and R6 does not reach it.
counterSignals: The exact-product positioning is protein- and oil-led ('reich an Antioxidantien, Fettsäuren', 'verbessert sichtbar die Haarstruktur') and the list carries five protein species — a strong claim/formula divergence. Recorded per §9.3 ('Protein naming with the protein only in the tail → moisture, with the claim recorded'); it never moves the value.

The whole call rests on tail_index = 6. A reviewer who instead took the preservative block (DMDM Hydantoin @24) as the marker would place five proteins above the tail and reach `protein` or `balanced` — a two-step swing. This is the single largest tail-rule sensitivity in the cohort (AP-01-TAILSWING).
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight, so even a credited hydrolysed protein could only support 'a protein film route is present'.
D4 protein-payload counter-signal did NOT fire here despite five protein species, because its detection threshold is above-tail-gated (AP-D4-BLINDSPOT).

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied (rich R1+R4 base does not create a focus). Step 2 mechanism grouping: the entire above-tail set is one M1 observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 above tail, no bond); `curl_support` blocked (no curl positioning and slip is baseline); `color_care` blocked (no candidate, no positioning); `lightness` blocked (weight_potential is `high`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked (zero humectants above the tail). Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1 fails outright). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected (see below). Step 7 `detangling` rejected. thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no specific focus clears the differentiator threshold and the formula evidence is nonspecific.

`smoothing` (the closest competitor) does not apply: step 6 is a conjunction. The second conjunct is arguably met — Lanolin @3 is a substantial emollient route beyond baseline — but the first is not: dry surface control is not this formula's clearest practical differentiator, because the only route beyond the base is a softening occlusive, with no silicone, no substantive polymer, and no film former above the tail.

`detangling` does not apply: §9.5.2 step 7 permits it only when slip is itself distinctive. Two cationics above the tail is the category's own baseline-to-slightly-above band, and the 'entwirrt' claim can corroborate but never create (step 9).

adjudicationPoints.title: CLOSED by E1 (2026-09-14) — the tail-edge strike is withdrawn and this product's conditioning_level returns to `high`
adjudicationPoints.body: Raised under v0.2: applying R3's tail-edge exclusion as written dropped this product from `high` to `moderate` because QUATERNIUM-18 @5 sat exactly at tail_index − 1 (PARFUM @6), which contradicted the ruling ledger's 'five evidence-backed highs stand' arithmetic. Nick ruled E1 on 2026-09-14: the ledger's reading governs and the mechanism was wrong. A boundary-position species counts normally; the boundary uncertainty is a confidence matter, because relative order above the marker is legally reliable under Art. 19 and only the 1 % line is invisible, and because ~1 % of a co-conditioning quat is a functional dose rather than a decorative trace. conditioning_level therefore returns to `high` at `moderate` confidence, with the dependence recorded as a `boundary_position_ingredient` hinweise note. Nothing further is needed from Nick on this record.
adjudicationPoints.source: §9.1 boundary-position rule (E1, 2026-09-14); plans/mask-inci/round1-rule-rulings.md, Escalation rulings (round-1b), E1

assumptionNotes: Re-derived under v0.3 (E1 boundary-position rule, replacing R3's tail-edge exclusion; E2 third plausibility limb checked and not fired; E4 checked against weight_potential and not engaging), not patched — §12 G7 and §15 both require re-derivation, and no v0.2 field approval or fingerprint carries forward.

Fields whose value moved under v0.3: conditioningLevel (moderate → high, E1; confidence held at moderate by the boundary cap). Fields whose evidence text was re-derived under a changed rule: conditioningLevel (E1), damageFit (echo of the moved driver — output set unchanged because §9.7 rows 2 and 3 are identical), tailMarker (E2 limb checked). weightPotential was re-checked under E4 and does NOT move: the `low` leanness test fails at its first conjunct on LANOLIN @3, an R4b heavy lipid above the marker, so `high` stands on the unchanged R4 anchor. Every other field carries its v0.2 value and text.

Review triggers under v0.3 — FIRED: none newly. NOT fired: `tail_marker_anomaly` (marker present), `tail_marker_unresolved` (marker plausible on all three §3.1.1 limbs, including E2's new one), `protein_payload_review` (the payload is tail-side, so §13.1's `protein_tail_only` note applies instead and it may not fire a trigger of its own), `bond_claim_review`, `low_confidence_field` (no field at `low` confidence — the boundary dependence caps at `moderate`, it does not step down), `weight_high_conflict`, `specialist_damage_fit`.

fired.value: QUATERNIUM-18 @5, one rank above tail_index 6 (PARFUM); load-bearing for conditioning_level
fired.note: conditioning_level `high` hinges on a boundary-position ingredient: S1 fires only because QUATERNIUM-18 @5 is counted as the second distinct cationic, and it sits at tail_index − 1. Without it the value would be `moderate`. Under E1 (2026-09-14) the species counts in full — relative order above the marker is reliable, only the invisible 1 % line is not — and the uncertainty is carried here and as the field's `moderate` confidence cap. This note moves no value. No other field on this record hinges on it: weight_potential rests on LANOLIN @3 and care_direction on the absence of any above-tail R5 species.

fired.note: Four protein species, plus SILK AMINO ACIDS @12 and SODIUM LAUROYL OAT AMINO ACIDS @14, are declared at or after the tail marker. The payload is present and carries zero classification credit (§3.1, §13.1 rule 3): it contributes nothing to care_direction, repair_support_level, damage_fit or the repair focus, and it is not a D4 payload either, since D4 counts above-tail species. Recorded so a reviewer who sees the proteins on the pack and in the list can see that the engine saw them too, and why they earned nothing. This flag caps no confidence and moves no value.

v0AdjudicationPointStatus.AP-01-LANOLIN: CLOSED by R8. Lexicon family 3 now lists Lanolin and its derivatives in the heavy band explicitly, so the R4b reading is lexicon-backed rather than a reviewer judgment. `weight_potential: high` no longer rests on a hinge.
v0AdjudicationPointStatus.AP-01-TAILSWING: CLOSED by E1 (was PARTLY CLOSED under v0.2). The marker is formally assessed (plausible on all three §3.1.1 limbs) and the boundary-band species is handled exactly as v0.1's reviewer policy proposed — as a confidence modifier that never moves a value. The residual band-width question survives only as a low-stakes calibration item (§9.1, E1): no width of band strikes anything any more.
v0AdjudicationPointStatus.AP-D4-BLINDSPOT: STILL LIVE — carried forward unchanged from reference-key-v0; R8's `protein_tail_only` flag now makes the tail payload visible on the review surface, which is a partial answer.
v0AdjudicationPointStatus.AP-G0-PLACEMENT: CLOSED by R8. Placement is no longer a G0 conjunct; unstated placement defaults to the P5 canonical placement and the product stays eligible.
